angle: SendX's homepage evolution is a study in what happens when a challenger tool in a crowded category runs out of room to differentiate on features and price — and bets everything on one defensible metric: inbox placement. The defining moment is not the H1 rewrite but the 2021 removal of 'Feature-Rich' that preceded it.
distinct_from: H1 adjective reduction as a testable progression
h1: SendX Homepage Teardown: How an Email Tool Stopped Listing Features and Started Proving Inbox Placement

sections.goal: Open with the H1 contrast: 'Intuitive, Feature-Rich, Affordable' → 'Send unlimited emails. Land in the inbox. That's it.' Name the proof point (95–98% inbox placement, 4.4B emails) in the intro. Tell the reader they will learn what drives a company to simplify rather than expand.

sections.custom_h2: ## SendX's homepage arc 2019–2026: from feature catalogue to inbox-placement proof
sections.goal: Show three phases: 2019 feature-catalogue H2s (Send Campaigns, Build List, Automate); 2021 quiet H1 simplification (Feature-Rich removed); 2026 deliverability-first with proof denominator. The progression shows the simplification was deliberate, not sudden.

sections.custom_h2: ## How SendX's homepage messaging shifted from feature breadth to inbox placement proof
sections.goal: Analyze: H1 shift (adjectives→outcomes), meta description shift (feature list→deliverability proof with denominator), and H2 'Ready to make email work again?' as a competitor-migration signal. Explain what each change assumes about the visitor's awareness of their deliverability problem.

sections.custom_h2: ## How SendX's CTAs and navigation changed the sales motion
sections.goal: Analyze: demo CTA removal (self-serve bet), 'START FREE TRIAL NOW' all-caps → 'Start Free 14 Day Trial' (urgency → specificity), feature 'Explore' CTAs as product-led discovery. Nav expansion from minimal (HOME, Book DEMO) to product-indexed. End with nav test.

sections.custom_h2: ## Why SendX stopped competing on features and started competing on inbox placement
sections.goal: Explain the Mailchimp acquisition/upmarket move, Klaviyo's ecommerce claim, Brevo's SMB CRM claim — and how deliverability became the last defensible differentiator. Explain what 'Ready to make email work again?' implies about the target buyer (churned from Mailchimp).

sections.custom_h2: ## What SaaS teams can study from SendX's homepage evolution
sections.goal: 3 patterns: (1) adjective-removal as a testable path to H1 simplification; (2) proof denominators making specific claims credible; (3) competitor-migration section heading. Each must have a specific runnable test.
